data.narrative:
Helion Energy is a Series F nuclear energy company with total raised capital exceeding $1B. The current valuation of $15.5B sits significantly above comparable peers in the frontier nuclear sector. The comp universe includes 3 public companies (Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, and an entity trading under SMR) and 5 private-stage firms including Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the last post-money round of $5.4B and applies a typical Series F step-up multiplier of 1.3x, yielding $7.0B. Peer-median analysis across 3 same-sector comparables with similar valuation tiers produces a median of $6.0B, with a range spanning $5.6B (X-Energy) to $7.0B (Oklo). The peer set reflects stage diversity—mixing public and pre-IPO private firms—which introduces some comparability noise but anchors within the nuclear energy sector.

Triangulation across these two methods implies a valuation range of $5.1B to $8.1B, with a median of $6.5B. The current $15.5B valuation exceeds this analytically supported range by 2.4x, reflecting either a significant private-market premium, optionality not captured in peer comparables, or a valuation reset in the near term. Key uncertainties include stage-comparable discount rates, X-Energy and Valar Atomics' actual post-money figures, and whether public nuclear comps trade at meaningful stage-related discounts to late-stage private counterparts.
